problem: VLMs for embodied QA take a fixed, finite set of input views and answer in one step, so they cannot actively acquire question-relevant context that is occluded or spread across viewpoints. The many redundant frames also dilute the useful information.
motivation: EQA questions often need multi-step reasoning and world knowledge (e.g. 'where can I get pop drinks?' means finding a refrigerator), which a one-shot answer over fixed views cannot deliver. Test-time reasoning (CoT, budget forcing) helps LLMs without training, so the authors ask whether the same idea works for viewpoint acquisition in 3D scenes.
key_idea: Turn a VLM into an active viewpoint reasoner: first select question-aligned anchor views, then interleave reasoning with discrete camera actions (SE(3) moves and rotations) that render new views from the 3D scene until enough evidence is gathered.
insight: Both stages matter. Removing coarse view selection lowers the CoV(3 step) score on all four VLMs, by an average of 4.59%; for example GLM-4.6v drops from 67.20 to 62.43. Performance also improves with a larger minimum action budget (average +2.51%), so budget forcing gives a form of test-time scaling. Without a forced budget most questions stop after 1-3 steps, and questions that use more steps score higher.
method: View Selection Agent: the VLM sees all frames (sampled at 10:1 from the video) with their indices plus the question, and outputs the IDs of relevant frames, giving a subset V' with K much smaller than T. A bird's-eye view of the scene is also provided.

CoV Agent action loop: starting from an anchor view, at each step the VLM reasons over the current observation and the question and emits a discrete action. The new observation is appended to the context.

Action space: 6 translations (forward/back/left/right/up/down), rotations (yaw, pitch, roll), and switching to any selected anchor view. Each action is converted to an SE(3) transform that updates the camera pose, and the new view is rendered from the 3D scene representation.

Termination and budget forcing: the loop stops when the agent judges the information sufficient or a step limit is reached. A minimum number of action steps is enforced through the prompt, inspired by s1, to obtain test-time scaling.
Model-agnostic, training-free design: the same underlying VLM plays both the selection and CoV agents, with the temperature fixed at 0.

setting.backbone: Frozen VLMs: Qwen3-VL-Flash, GLM-4.6V, Gemini-2.5-Flash, GPT-4o-mini (OpenEQA); GPT-4.1, Gemini Flash and InternVL (ScanQA/SQA3D)
setting.observation: Multi-view RGB(-D) frames with camera poses sampled from scene videos, plus a bird-eye view; novel views rendered from the 3D scene (mesh/point cloud)
setting.action_space: Discrete camera actions: 6 translations, yaw/pitch/roll rotations, view switch (rigid-body SE(3) transforms)
setting.simulator: Rendering from reconstructed 3D scenes (ScanNet / HM3D scenes in OpenEQA, ScanQA, SQA3D); no interactive simulator
setting.privileged: Reconstructed 3D scene representation with camera poses, used to render new views

numbers.extra: training-free; minimum action steps 4 (best); CoV(1 Step) gives 58.75; baseline 52.65

results: On OpenEQA, CoV improves all four VLMs, by 8.50-13.62% and an average of 11.56%, with the largest gain on Qwen3-VL-Flash (52.65 to 59.82 with the best minimum step count). Raising the minimum action steps adds a further 2.51% on average, peaking at 3.73% on Gemini-2.5-Flash. On ScanQA, CoV reaches 116 CIDEr and 31.9 EM@1 without training, above LEO (101.4 CIDEr) and Scene-LLM (27.2 EM@1). On SQA3D it gets 51.1 EM@1, below Chat-3D v2 (54.7) and ChatScene (54.6).
limitations: Long action trajectories can introduce noise or hallucination, and the approach may struggle in highly dynamic or cluttered scenes.
Accuracy depends on the quality of view selection, and a poor anchor view hurts reasoning.
Extra inference cost from multiple VLM calls is not analyzed. Comparisons use only a few weaker VLMs and no strong active-exploration baselines. The SQA3D result does not beat the trained 3D LMMs.
compares_to: Baseline VLM with all frames in one pass
